title: Intel Nova Lake Desktop CPU to Debut New Core Architecture Before Data Centers
excerpt: Intel confirms its next-generation Coyote Cove P-core will launch first on desktop Nova Lake-S processors, featuring a powerful 12-core Xe3P integrated GPU aimed at challenging AMD's APU dominance.
body:
• Intel's Nova Lake-S desktop CPUs will be the first to use the new Coyote Cove P-core architecture, arriving before Diamond Rapids server chips.
  • A dedicated SKU with 12 Xe3P integrated graphics cores and a 40W GPU power budget targets AMD's Ryzen APU lineup.
  • The desktop platform moves to a new LGA 1954 socket, which Intel plans to support across multiple CPU generations.
  • Nova Lake-S scales up to 52 cores in dual-tile configurations, with total cache reaching 288 MB on top-end models.

Intel has confirmed that its upcoming Nova Lake desktop processor family will be the first to feature the company's new Coyote Cove performance cores, marking a departure from the typical practice of debuting new architectures in data center chips first. The announcement, detailed in Intel's latest ISA reference update, provides the clearest public signal yet about the chipmaker's roadmap through late 2026 and into 2027.

A Desktop-First Strategy

Nova Lake-S pairs Coyote Cove P-cores with Arctic Wolf E-cores across a lineup that scales from 6-core entry-level chips at 35W up to 52-core, dual-tile flagships at 175W. The decision to prioritize desktop over Intel's Diamond Rapids Xeon server line — which will use the separate Panther Cove P-core — reflects a deliberate push to recapture consumer mindshare.

https://x.com/TechPowerUp/status/2089294371061395940

"Intel hopes enthusiasts 'do the math' compared to AMD."

— Robert Hallock, Intel VP

Intel VP Robert Hallock has publicly stated the company wants desktop enthusiasts to benchmark Nova Lake against AMD's competing Ryzen lineup, signaling confidence in the new core's IPC and performance-per-watt improvements over the previous Cougar Cove and Darkmont designs.

Integrated Graphics Get Serious

The most eye-catching detail is a specific Nova Lake-S SKU featuring 12 Xe3P integrated graphics cores — a significant upgrade from the standard 2 Xe3 cores found in the rest of the lineup. This chip, configured with 4 P-cores, 8 E-cores, and 4 low-power E-cores for a total of 16 cores, dedicates a substantial 40W power budget solely to its GPU tile, with total chip power reaching 154W at PL2.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=J_wVrj-nouY

The Xe3P architecture, internally codenamed Celestial, represents a generational leap from Xe3. Early benchmarks suggest Intel's Xe3 already holds a significant lead over AMD's RDNA 3.5 in mainstream integrated graphics, with advantages approaching 2x in some workloads. The beefier Xe3P variant could position Intel to compete directly with AMD's Ryzen APUs, which have long dominated the budget gaming and content creation segments.

Platform and Lineup Details

Nova Lake-S introduces the LGA 1954 socket, replacing the current LGA 1851. Intel has indicated it will support this socket across multiple CPU generations, aligning with AMD's consumer-friendly platform strategy and breaking from the company's long-criticized practice of single-generation socket cycles.

The full lineup spans from a 6-core Core Ultra 3 at 65W through mid-range Core Ultra 5 and Core Ultra 7 chips up to dual-tile Core Ultra 9 and Core Ultra X models. Top-end SKUs feature Intel's Big Last Level Cache technology with up to 288 MB of total cache, directly targeting AMD's 3D V-Cache lineup.

What's Next

Nova Lake-S is expected to launch in the second half of 2026 or early 2027. Intel is also developing higher-end "Halo" mobile SKUs and a custom silicon design with NVIDIA that will house discrete RTX graphics tiles, broadening its GPU-heavy product portfolio. For now, the desktop-first approach signals Intel's renewed commitment to the enthusiast market after years of ceding ground to AMD.
